problems.title: False sharing
problems.statement: Two counters in the same cache line, each incremented by its own core 10⁸ times.

options: the line ping-pongs between cores: often 10×+ slower than separate lines

hints: Coherence works on lines, not variables.

problems.title: ABA
problems.statement: A lock-free stack pop: read top = A, next = B; another thread pops A, pops B, pushes A back; the first thread's CAS(top, A → B) succeeds.

options: top now points to B, which was popped (maybe freed)
tagged pointer with a version counter

problems.title: Throughput
problems.statement: 4 producers CAS the same tail; each successful CAS moves the line (~80 ns transfer).

parts.prompt: Upper bound on successful pushes per second (millions, 1 / 80 ns)?

problems.solution: At most about 12.5M/s regardless of core count; per-producer rings remove the shared write.

problems.title: Progress guarantees

parts.prompt: A CAS-loop queue where some thread always succeeds:
An SPSC ring where each op finishes in bounded steps:

problems.solution: Lock-free means system-wide progress; wait-free means per-thread bounded progress.

problems.title: Cached indices
problems.statement: In the SPSC ring, the producer keeps a local copy of head and re-reads the atomic only when the copy says "full".

options: far fewer reads of the consumer's cache line, so less coherence traffic

hints: Each cross-core read can pull the line.
problems.solution: Most pushes then touch only the producer's own line and the slot.

problems.title: Spin waiting
problems.statement: A pinned consumer busy-polls an empty ring.

options: isolate the core (isolcpus) so nothing else runs there

problems.solution: Yielding reintroduces scheduler latency; pause eases pipeline and power pressure.
